html:
The Netherlands is a small, flat country on the North Sea, much of it land won from the sea and below sea level. On the map from 1715 it holds the European homeland, and in Africa the Cape and trading forts on the Gold Coast.

In 1715 it was still the Dutch Republic, a federation of provinces that had broken away from Spain in the late 1500s. In the 1600s Amsterdam had been the hub of world trade, with the Dutch East India Company in Asia and the Amsterdam exchange at home. The company settled the Cape in 1652 to supply its ships.

Its later story:

  • 1795: the French turned it into the Batavian Republic, and Napoleon later annexed it.
  • 1806: the Cape was lost for good to Britain.
  • 1815: it became a kingdom, joined with Belgium until the Belgians broke away in 1830.
  • 1848: a new constitution made it a parliamentary democracy.
  • 1872: it sold its Gold Coast forts to Britain.

It stayed neutral in the First World War, but Germany occupied it from 1940 to 1945; most Dutch Jews, among them Anne Frank, were murdered. It lost its largest colony, the Netherlands Indies, when Indonesia won independence by 1949. After a flood in 1953 killed some 1,800 people it built the Delta Works of dams and barriers. It was a founder of the European communities in 1957.
